stories.title: McKinsey 'State of Organizations 2026': 88% of Enterprises Deploy AI, 88% See No Bottom-Line Impact
stories.body: McKinsey's State of Organizations 2026 report (surveying 10,018 executives) finds that 88% of organizations now use AI in at least one business function, yet only 39% report measurable EBIT impact — and 86% of leaders say their organizations are not prepared to adopt AI in day-to-day operations. The top three barriers cited are concerns about AI itself (46%), regulatory or ethical concerns (44%), and organizational change management challenges (39%). In the US alone, only 1% of C-suite respondents describe their generative AI rollouts as mature.
stories.why: This is the definitive proof point for why retail AI pilots stall: it's a coordination and readiness gap, not a capability gap — exactly the conversation a Graas seller should be having with any CIO or CDO. The 86% unpreparedness figure reframes the sales conversation from 'do you need AI?' to 'do you have the data and organizational foundation to make it work?' — which is Graas's core value proposition.

stories.tag: US - analyst research / CPG-retail AI scaling
stories.title: BCG & Consumer Goods Forum Report: 75% of CPGs Still in Pilot Mode, Agentic AI Could Deliver Up to 350bps EBIT
stories.body: A BCG and Consumer Goods Forum survey of 39 senior CPG and retail executives worldwide ('AI in CPG and Retail: How Winners Are Pulling Ahead') finds roughly 75% of CPG companies remain in pilot or exploration mode, with only 18% achieving scaled impact. More than half of surveyed companies do not formally measure the ROI of their AI investments. BCG calculates that scaling AI initiatives across the demand value chain could deliver 220–350 basis points of cumulative EBIT for CPGs and 180–360 bps for retailers, with agentic capabilities potentially expanding that opportunity up to 1.7x over the next two to three years.
stories.why: The 'pilot purgatory' finding is a direct conversation-opener: if 75% of CPG prospects are stuck in pilots, the question is what's blocking them — and the answer is almost always fragmented data and lack of a governed context layer before agents are deployed. The 350bps EBIT opportunity gives sellers a defensible ROI anchor for the architecture investment conversation.

stories.tag: US - enterprise AI architecture / context layer
stories.title: Forrester: 'Build Meaning Before Machines' — Ontologies and Knowledge Graphs Are Now Core Agentic AI Infrastructure
stories.body: A Forrester blog post argues that when agents lack semantic grounding they misinterpret metrics, get joins wrong, and act on flawed assumptions — making ontologies, semantic layers, and knowledge graphs 'rapidly becoming core architectural components.' Forrester proposes a layered approach in which ontologies define knowledge, semantics enforce consistency, and knowledge graphs connect these elements into a model that supports reasoning; it positions the semantic layer as the right starting point for most organizations, with the knowledge graph as the long-term destination and 'a form of digital twin that enables agentic AI to reason and act across the enterprise.' Independent 2026 benchmarks on retail analytics data show adding explicit business semantics raises LLM accuracy by 17–23 percentage points across frontier models.
stories.why: Forrester naming semantics + ontology + knowledge graph as the prerequisite infrastructure for agentic AI is analyst cover for every Graas 'context layer first' pitch. Sellers can cite this directly to CIOs who are skeptical of spending on data foundations before deploying agents — especially when paired with the 17–23 point accuracy lift from retail-specific benchmark data.

stories.title: Sierra Hits $400M ARR and $15.8B Valuation; Salesforce Acquires Fin (Intercom) for $3.6B; Zendesk Absorbs Forethought
stories.body: Sierra raised a $950 million Series E in May 2026 at a $15.8 billion post-money valuation led by GV and Tiger Global, and announced in October 2026 it had surpassed $400 million in ARR — adding more than $150 million in Q3 alone. Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin (formerly Intercom) for approximately $3.6 billion on September 10, 2026, with Fin at roughly $400 million ARR at time of closing; Fin continues to price at $0.99 per outcome inside the Salesforce stack. Zendesk separately completed its acquisition of Forethought in March 2026 and launched a Resolution Platform with outcome-based pricing, ending Forethought's run as an independent vendor.
stories.why: Three major consolidation moves in one quarter reshapes the competitive landscape: Fin is now a Salesforce-bundled product (changing the enterprise buying motion), Forethought is gone as a standalone option, and Sierra's $400M ARR at a ~40x multiple signals investors believe agentic CX is winner-take-most. Graas sellers need to know which of these vendors they will encounter in a deal and how the new ownership structures affect procurement, pricing, and lock-in risk.

stories.tag: US - named deployment / CPG supply chain agents
stories.title: BCG: Agentic AI Boosts In-Stocks 2–4% and Planning Productivity Over 60% in CPG–Retailer Supply Chain Pilots
stories.body: BCG published a detailed playbook ('Breaking Friction Silos') documenting that in pilots with large CPG manufacturers and retailers, agentic AI unlocked 2–4% improvements in in-stock rates and more than 60% gains in planning productivity by replacing asynchronous, fragmented decision-making across retailer buyers, replenishment planners, and CPG sales analysts. BCG's supply chain agent architecture is built around a curated action ontology for supply chain processes and an agentic harness design for reliability — both prerequisites to deploying multi-agent replenishment workflows. A separate BCG Executive Perspectives paper (May 2026) documents a global CPG leader that redesigned replenishment from reactive to proactive using an agentic platform, shifting to a live collaboration workflow with retailers.
stories.why: This is the closest thing to a named enterprise deployment with hard outcome numbers available from a credible source this month — and BCG explicitly calls out a 'curated action ontology' as the design foundation, which is the same architecture argument Graas makes. The 60%+ planning productivity lift is a quotable outcome for supply chain or merchandising conversations with retail and CPG accounts.
